bayts.text: I have revived (by celebrating it) the Mawlid of the Prophet (Muḥammad) since the year Asash (1301 H / 1883-84), and what surpasses all wishes yielded to me in the year Hamsash (1345 H / 1926-27).
God has taught me of what He wills; and so Iblīs (Satan) fled, together with whoever followed him.
On Thursday, in the month of Rajab, (God) came to meet me with what endures forever, the best of wonders.
God, Creator of creatures and of time, has defended what I sold (to Him) from going to others, together with its price.
The Most Holy (Al-Quddūs) has freed me from my illnesses, and has placed the Greatest (al-Aʿẓam) within my aims.
When I write or recite, there comes to me what fulfils hope.
There remains, between me and my Lord, no turbidity; and He has led me with love.
There remains, between me and the Chosen One (Muḥammad) — God's blessing be upon him — no obstacle to ascent.
God is my Lord, my Intimate Friend and the Beloved; and the Chosen One (Muḥammad) is my means, intimate friend, beloved.
Iblīs (Satan), my bane, has fled towards others than me, together with his tribe; and my pearls grow.
The Bestower of benefit (An-Nāfiʿ) has extended to me an immense benefit, and has thrust towards others than me whoever grew proud.
I have intended to give thanks to God through the Book (the Qur'an), and God has kept me from reproach.
My wonder (karāma) is the writing of my hand; and through my writing my Lord has drawn to me the greatest of them, and he allowed himself to be drawn.
He who grants Revelation (Allah) has instructed me in writing, and the Giver of life (Al-Muḥyī) has guarded my life for the Gardens.
He has instructed me, purified my inmost being, kept my whole being safe, while before Him I give thanks for the pen.
The pens have joined me to the noble hosts, and through them God has led to me the most excellent of goals.
My writing has driven the enemies of God towards other than my horizons, and I have triumphed through His bounties (ālāʾ).
(God) has raised what I have written since the year Asash (1301 H / 1883-84), giving notice of its raising in the year Hamsash (1345 H / 1926-27).
